title: Acts Chapter 3 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Acts chapter 3 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Acts Chapter 3 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Acts Chapter 3.

questions.question: In Acts 3, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Peter and John went up to the temple
A certain man lame from his mother's womb was carried
The man entered the temple walking and praising God
questions.correctAnswer: Peter and John went up to the temple
questions.explanation: This event is described in Acts 3:1, where it states that Peter and John went up together into the temple.

questions.question: Who was carried to the gate of the temple?
options: A certain man lame from his mother's womb
questions.correctAnswer: A certain man lame from his mother's womb
questions.explanation: Acts 3:2 specifies that a certain man lame from his mother's womb was carried to the gate of the temple.

questions.question: What was the name of the gate where the lame man was laid?
questions.explanation: According to Acts 3:2, the gate of the temple was called Beautiful.

questions.question: What did the lame man ask for from Peter and John?
questions.explanation: Acts 3:3 states that the lame man asked for alms from Peter and John as they entered the temple.

questions.question: What did Peter tell the lame man to do?
questions.explanation: In Acts 3:4, Peter said to the lame man, 'Look on us.'

questions.question: What did the lame man expect to receive from Peter and John?
questions.explanation: Acts 3:5 indicates that the lame man gave heed, expecting to receive something of them, implying he was expecting to receive money.

questions.question: What did Peter say he did not have?
questions.explanation: In Acts 3:6, Peter states, 'Silver and gold have I none.'

questions.question: What did Peter offer to the lame man?
questions.explanation: Acts 3:6 shows Peter saying, 'but such as I have give I thee,' referring to healing in the name of Jesus Christ.

questions.question: What happened to the lame man when Peter lifted him up?
options: His feet and ankle bones received strength
questions.correctAnswer: His feet and ankle bones received strength
questions.explanation: Acts 3:7 states that when Peter lifted him up, 'immediately his feet and ankle bones received strength.'

questions.question: What did the lame man do after he was healed?
questions.explanation: Acts 3:8 describes that the man, after being healed, 'leaping up stood, and walked.'

questions.question: What did the healed man do as he entered the temple?
questions.explanation: Acts 3:8 states that the man entered the temple 'walking, and leaping, and praising God.'

questions.question: Did all the people see the healed man?
questions.explanation: Acts 3:9 confirms that all the people saw him walking and praising God.

questions.question: Did Peter and John go to the temple for the hour of prayer?
questions.explanation: Acts 3:1 indicates that Peter and John went to the temple at the hour of prayer, which was the ninth hour.

questions.question: The lame man was healed after he asked for food.
questions.explanation: The text does not say the lame man asked for food; he asked for alms according to Acts 3:3.

questions.question: Peter had a lot of silver and gold to give to the lame man.
questions.explanation: Acts 3:6 clearly states that Peter said, 'Silver and gold have I none.'

medium.title: Acts Chapter 3 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Acts Chapter 3 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What were the people filled with after witnessing the healing of the lame man?
questions.explanation: The people were filled with wonder and amazement at that which had happened unto him. (Acts 3:10)

questions.question: What does Acts 3:10 promise will happen if someone experiences a miracle?
options: They will be filled with wonder and amazement
questions.correctAnswer: They will be filled with wonder and amazement
questions.explanation: Acts 3:10 shows that experiencing a miracle leads to wonder and amazement among the people.

questions.question: Who did the lame man hold onto after being healed?
questions.explanation: The lame man which was healed held Peter and John. (Acts 3:11)

questions.question: What did Peter ask the people in Acts 3:12?
questions.explanation: Peter asked the people 'Why marvel ye at this?' in response to their wonder. (Acts 3:12)

questions.question: What did Peter attribute the healing of the lame man to in Acts 3:16?
questions.explanation: Peter stated that the name through faith in his name hath made this man strong. (Acts 3:16)

questions.question: According to Acts 3:17, who did Peter say acted out of ignorance?
questions.explanation: Peter acknowledged that through ignorance, the men of Israel did it. (Acts 3:17)

questions.question: What does Acts 3:18 say about what God had shown through the prophets?
questions.explanation: Acts 3:18 reveals that God had shown through the prophets that Christ should suffer.

questions.question: What does the healing of the lame man illustrate about faith according to Acts 3?
options: Faith is only for the wealthy
questions.explanation: The healing of the lame man illustrates that faith in Jesus can lead to miraculous healing. (Acts 3:16)

questions.question: How did the crowd react to the healing of the lame man?
questions.explanation: The crowd was greatly wondering after witnessing the miracle. (Acts 3:11)

questions.question: What role does Peter claim he and John had in the healing in Acts 3:12?
questions.explanation: Peter clarified that it was not by their own power or holiness that the man was healed. (Acts 3:12)

questions.question: What did Peter emphasize about Jesus in Acts 3:15?
options: He was the Prince of life
questions.correctAnswer: He was the Prince of life
questions.explanation: Peter referred to Jesus as the Prince of life, whom God raised from the dead. (Acts 3:15)

questions.question: What is one lesson about confession and repentance found in Acts 3?
questions.explanation: Peter's public address to the crowd indicates the importance of public confession and repentance. (Acts 3:12)

questions.question: Is it true that Peter and John had money to give to the lame man?
questions.explanation: Peter stated, 'Silver and gold have I none.' (Acts 3:6)

questions.question: Is it true that the healing of the lame man was witnessed by many people?
questions.explanation: The healing was witnessed by all the people who saw him walking and praising God. (Acts 3:9)

questions.question: Is it true that Peter blamed the rulers for the healing of the lame man?
questions.explanation: Peter acknowledged that the men of Israel, including their rulers, acted out of ignorance. (Acts 3:17)

hard.title: Acts Chapter 3 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Acts Chapter 3.

questions.question: According to Acts 3:19, what must happen so that your sins may be blotted out?
options: Repent ye therefore, and be converted
questions.correctAnswer: Repent ye therefore, and be converted
questions.explanation: Acts 3:19 states that repentance and conversion are required for sins to be blotted out.

questions.question: In Acts 3:20, who is said to be sent by God after repentance?
questions.explanation: Acts 3:20 clearly states that God shall send Jesus Christ after repentance.

questions.question: What does Acts 3:21 say heaven must do until the times of restitution of all things?
questions.explanation: Acts 3:21 states that heaven must receive Jesus until the times of restitution of all things.

questions.question: According to Acts 3:22, who does Moses say God will raise up?
questions.explanation: Acts 3:22 quotes Moses saying God will raise up a prophet like unto him.

questions.question: What consequence is mentioned in Acts 3:23 for those who will not hear the prophet?
options: They shall be destroyed from among the people
They shall be exiled to a foreign land
They shall be cursed with famine
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be destroyed from among the people
questions.explanation: Acts 3:23 states that souls who do not hear the prophet shall be destroyed from among the people.

questions.question: In Acts 3:26, for what purpose was Jesus sent to bless the people?
options: In turning away every one from his iniquities
questions.correctAnswer: In turning away every one from his iniquities
questions.explanation: Acts 3:26 states Jesus was sent to bless the people by turning them away from their iniquities.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'metanoeite' in Acts 3:19 mean?
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'metanoeite' translated as 'repent' means to change one's mind or purpose, as seen in Acts 3:19.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Acts 3:19-21 to emphasize restoration and hope?
questions.explanation: Acts 3:19-21 uses inclusio framing with repentance and restoration themes to bracket the section, emphasizing hope.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage does Acts 3:22 directly quote about a prophet like Moses?
questions.explanation: Acts 3:22 quotes Deuteronomy 18:15 about a prophet like Moses to be raised up by God.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of Jesus as the Prophet and fulfillment of prophecy seen in Acts 3:22-23?
questions.explanation: John 6:14 recognizes Jesus as the Prophet like unto Moses, echoing Acts 3:22-23's theme.

questions.question: What event precedes Peter telling the crowd to repent in Acts 3:19?
options: Healing of the lame man at the temple gate
questions.correctAnswer: Healing of the lame man at the temple gate
questions.explanation: In Acts 3:1-18, Peter heals the lame man before calling the crowd to repentance in 3:19.

questions.question: What type of prophecy fulfillment is described in Acts 3:18 regarding Christ's suffering?
questions.explanation: Acts 3:18 shows Christ's suffering fulfills typological and predictive prophecies as revealed by God's prophets.

questions.question: Acts 3:25 calls believers 'children of the prophets.' This suggests a literary device of:
options: Typology linking New Covenant believers to Old Testament promises
questions.correctAnswer: Typology linking New Covenant believers to Old Testament promises
questions.explanation: Acts 3:25 uses typology to link believers to the covenant promises made to the prophets and Abraham.

questions.question: True or False: Acts 3:24 indicates that only Samuel foretold the coming days of Christ.
questions.explanation: Acts 3:24 says all the prophets from Samuel and those after him foretold these days, not only Samuel.

questions.question: True or False: Acts 3:26 teaches that God raised Jesus to bless the people by turning them away from their sins.
questions.explanation: Acts 3:26 explicitly states Jesus was sent to bless by turning people away from iniquities.

theological.title: Acts Chapter 3 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Acts Chapter 3 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 3:6 teach about the nature of salvation?
options: Salvation is by faith in Jesus Christ alone, not by earthly riches.
Salvation can be earned through acts of charity and almsgiving.
Salvation depends on the possession of silver and gold.
Salvation requires the temple sacrifices to be effective.
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation is by faith in Jesus Christ alone, not by earthly riches.
questions.explanation: Acts 3:6 shows that Peter has no silver or gold to give, but heals in the name of Jesus Christ, teaching salvation and healing come through faith in Jesus, not material wealth.

questions.question: What doctrine regarding Christ’s resurrection is taught in Acts 3:15?
options: Jesus is the Prince of life, raised from the dead by God, affirming His divine authority over death.
Jesus’ resurrection was a metaphorical event understood only spiritually.
Jesus remained dead but lives on in the hearts of believers.
The resurrection was a human fabrication to inspire the disciples.
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus is the Prince of life, raised from the dead by God, affirming His divine authority over death.
questions.explanation: Acts 3:15 explicitly states God raised Jesus, the Prince of life, from the dead, affirming the historic and divine nature of the resurrection.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sin and ignorance is revealed in Acts 3:17?
options: Sin can be committed through ignorance, but it still has consequences needing repentance.
Ignorance absolves people from responsibility for sin.
Only rulers are accountable for sin, not the common people.
Sin is irrelevant if done unknowingly.
questions.correctAnswer: Sin can be committed through ignorance, but it still has consequences needing repentance.
questions.explanation: Acts 3:17 acknowledges that the people and rulers acted in ignorance, yet this does not remove the need for repentance.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 3:13 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Acts 3:13 references God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, showing God’s faithfulness to His covenant promises through Jesus.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated in Acts 3:21?
questions.explanation: Acts 3:21 proclaims that heaven must receive Jesus until the times of restitution, affirming God’s sovereign control over redemptive history.

questions.question: How does the healing of the lame man in Acts 3 prepare for the fulfillment of Old Testament messianic prophecy?
options: It demonstrates Jesus as the promised prophet like Moses who brings restoration.
It nullifies the need for any Old Testament prophecy.
It shows that healing is unrelated to messianic expectations.
It emphasizes the temple’s power over prophecy.
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates Jesus as the promised prophet like Moses who brings restoration.
questions.explanation: Acts 3:22-23 connects the healing event to Moses’ prophecy of a prophet like him, showing Jesus as the fulfillment.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme is advanced by Peter's call to repentance in Acts 3:19?
options: The necessity of repentance as a condition for receiving the times of refreshing and restoration.
The idea that repentance is optional to believers.
That repentance only benefits the individual without communal effects.
That repentance is a one-time event with no ongoing significance.
questions.correctAnswer: The necessity of repentance as a condition for receiving the times of refreshing and restoration.
questions.explanation: Acts 3:19 connects repentance with the promise of refreshed fellowship with God, a key theme in redemptive history.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 3:14 and 3:15 teach about human sin and divine justice?
options: Human rejection of the Holy One results in putting to death the Prince of life, but God’s justice is revealed in the resurrection.
Human sin is excused if done ignorantly.
God does not judge those who deny Jesus.
Divine justice is arbitrary and unrelated to human actions.
questions.correctAnswer: Human rejection of the Holy One results in putting to death the Prince of life, but God’s justice is revealed in the resurrection.
questions.explanation: Acts 3:14-15 show the people’s denial and killing of Jesus, yet God raised Him, revealing just judgment and mercy.

questions.question: What doctrine about Jesus’ prophetic role and judgment is synthesized in Acts 3:22-23?
options: Jesus is the prophet like Moses, and rejecting Him results in destruction.
Jesus is a minor prophet with no authority.
Only Moses is to be heard, not Jesus.
Prophecy is irrelevant for Christian faith.
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus is the prophet like Moses, and rejecting Him results in destruction.
questions.explanation: Acts 3:22-23 cites Moses’ prophecy, emphasizing Jesus’ role and the judgment for those who refuse to hear Him.

questions.question: What doctrine about the Abrahamic covenant and blessing is taught in Acts 3:25-26?
options: Jesus is the fulfillment of the promise to Abraham, bringing blessing by turning people from iniquity.
The Abrahamic covenant is replaced and no longer valid.
Blessings come apart from Jesus and the covenant.
The covenant only concerned material prosperity.
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus is the fulfillment of the promise to Abraham, bringing blessing by turning people from iniquity.
questions.explanation: Acts 3:25-26 connects Jesus’ sending to the covenant promise to Abraham to bless all families through repentance.

questions.question: Skeptics claim the healing was a mere coincidence or trick. What does Acts 3:1-10 teach that refutes this claim?
options: The man was known to be lame from birth and instantly healed, witnessed by all present.
Peter used sleight of hand to fake the healing.
The man only pretended to be lame to get alms.
The healing was delayed and doubtful.
questions.correctAnswer: The man was known to be lame from birth and instantly healed, witnessed by all present.
questions.explanation: Acts 3:1-10 describes the man’s lifelong condition and immediate healing, causing amazement and public testimony.

questions.question: What doctrine about faith and healing is taught in Acts 3:16?
options: Faith in Jesus’ name is the means of healing and strength, demonstrated publicly.
Healing is based on human effort alone.
Healing is a random act unrelated to faith.
questions.correctAnswer: Faith in Jesus’ name is the means of healing and strength, demonstrated publicly.
questions.explanation: Acts 3:16 states the man was made strong through faith in the name of Jesus, showing faith’s essential role.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is particularly highlighted in Acts 3:18 regarding suffering and prophecy?
options: Omniscience, as God foretold Christ’s suffering through prophets.
Wrath, because suffering is God’s punishment only.
Immutability, as God refuses to change His mind.
Jealousy, because God demands exclusive worship.
questions.correctAnswer: Omniscience, as God foretold Christ’s suffering through prophets.
questions.explanation: Acts 3:18 reveals God’s foreknowledge and sovereign plan to fulfill prophecy about Christ’s suffering.

questions.question: How do Acts 3:19 and 3:20 collectively teach about the eschatological hope for believers?
options: Repentance leads to times of refreshing and the sending of Jesus Christ, pointing to final restoration.
Eschatological hope is irrelevant to repentance.
Believers have no hope beyond this life.
Jesus will not return until all sin is eradicated by human effort.
questions.correctAnswer: Repentance leads to times of refreshing and the sending of Jesus Christ, pointing to final restoration.
questions.explanation: Acts 3:19-20 links repentance with the promised coming of Jesus and the times of refreshing, highlighting future hope.

questions.question: What doctrine about the nature of Jesus as the Messiah is taught in Acts 3:26?
options: Jesus was raised by God to bless and turn people from their sins.
Jesus was only a moral teacher without divine sending.
Jesus’ resurrection was symbolic but not real.
Jesus’ mission was limited to political liberation.
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus was raised by God to bless and turn people from their sins.
questions.explanation: Acts 3:26 states God raised His Son to bless and call people to repentance, defining Jesus’ messianic mission.
